memory_annotations.evidence_summary: Maya asked that Delta be included in Minneapolis carrier comparisons and favored when schedule and price are reasonably comparable, then selected the $548 Delta itinerary over a $476 American alternative because its timing was better.

messages.content: I need to sort out Philadelphia next. The workshop is Tuesday through Thursday in Center City, starting at 8:30 Tuesday and ending at 4:30 Thursday. I can leave Minneapolis after 3:30 Monday. Economy needs to stay under $700 round trip.

What dates are the Monday and Thursday, and do you want me to limit this to nonstops? The Thursday finish time will matter because Center City to PHL can take roughly 25–45 minutes by car depending on traffic, plus time to retrieve a bag if you leave one at the hotel.
Monday July 20 through Thursday July 23. Nonstop is strongly preferred, but show one-stop only if it solves a real schedule or price problem. I’ll have my suitcase with me at the workshop Thursday.

I found several nonstops within the allowance. The useful Monday departures are a Delta flight at 4:55 p.m., arriving PHL at 8:35 p.m., and an American flight at 5:30 p.m., arriving at 9:08 p.m. Both leave enough margin before Tuesday’s 8:30 start. For Thursday, the first practical choices after the workshop are American at 6:35 p.m. and Delta at 7:15 p.m.; the next nonstop is American at 8:20 p.m.
Is 6:35 actually workable after a 4:30 finish? I don’t want the itinerary to depend on everything going perfectly.

It is possible but tight. If you walk out at 4:30 and request a car immediately, a typical airport arrival would be around 5:05–5:25. That leaves 70–90 minutes before departure, but a workshop overrun, heavy traffic, or a slow security line could erase the cushion. I would treat 4:45 as the realistic car-departure target and avoid the 6:35 unless the savings are substantial.
Agreed. Use 4:45 leaving Center City and give me the Delta 7:15 plus the American 8:20. What do the Monday pairings cost?

With the current round-trip fares, the Delta 4:55 Monday paired with Delta’s 7:15 Thursday is $548. American’s 5:30 Monday paired with its 8:20 Thursday is $476. A mixed ticket using Delta outbound and American return prices at $631 because the legs ticket separately. All three are standard economy, nonstop, and below $700.

Include Delta when it works for these Minneapolis comparisons, and favor it when the schedule and price are reasonably close. Here the extra $72 seems acceptable for getting back an hour earlier. Is there any downside besides price?

The Delta pairing is the stronger fit here. Its Monday arrival is 33 minutes earlier and its Thursday return leaves 65 minutes earlier. The main downside is the $72 premium. The displayed Delta fare is nonrefundable after the 24-hour cancellation period, with changes allowed subject to any fare difference. Checked-bag charges are not included.
How much time does the 7:15 give me at PHL under that 4:45 plan? And when would I land in Minneapolis?

Leaving Center City at 4:45 should put you at PHL around 5:20–5:40 in ordinary weekday traffic, giving you about 1 hour 35 minutes to 1 hour 55 minutes before departure. The 7:15 p.m. nonstop is scheduled to arrive MSP at 9:18 p.m. Central Time.
That is option one. Keep the cheaper American itinerary as option two, and spell out both with the Thursday transfer assumptions. Don’t book either.

Option one: Delta nonstop, $548 round trip. Depart MSP Monday, July 20 at 4:55 p.m., arrive PHL at 8:35 p.m.; return Thursday, July 23 at 7:15 p.m., arrive MSP at 9:18 p.m. After the 4:30 workshop finish, leave Center City around 4:45 and expect to reach PHL at 5:20–5:40, leaving 95–115 minutes before departure.

Option two: American nonstop, $476 round trip. Depart MSP Monday at 5:30 p.m., arrive PHL at 9:08 p.m.; return Thursday at 8:20 p.m., arrive MSP at 10:23 p.m. The same transfer estimate leaves 160–180 minutes before departure.

Both are standard economy and within the $700 allowance. Delta is the recommended combination because the $72 difference buys earlier arrival in both directions while preserving a comfortable Thursday airport margin. Neither itinerary has been booked.

The Delta itinerary is recommended. Thursday’s transfer plan is to leave Center City at 4:45 p.m. after the 4:30 finish and reach PHL around 5:20–5:40 p.m.
